statement.p1: Every detail considered. Then lighting becomes an afterthought — and the architecture disappears.
statement.p2: We design light that reveals what you've already created. Not light you notice; light that makes the room, the material and the person inside it feel <it>inevitable.</it>

philosophy.body: We listen to what each space wants to be — then design light that helps it become that. Single, intentional sources over flooded rooms. Deliberate pools of shadow that make warmth feel warmer.
philosophy.sign: The architecture is the vision. Lighting serves it.

selected.side: The same studio that lights an art collector's home lights a tower, a beach house, a flagship, a jet.

range.side: The language changes. The discipline doesn't.
range.ramsaGo: Lighting that honours heritage and craftsmanship
range.elicyonGo: Lighting that celebrates line and transparency

tech.side: The light that feels like it was always there is the hardest kind to engineer. It takes more control, not less, to make light this calm.
tech.c1Title: A light that dims like a candle.
tech.c1Body: Most LEDs hold the same cold tone all the way down. The sources we specify warm as they dim — from clean white to the amber of a flame, the way daylight fades.
tech.c2Title: A house that keeps time with the sun.
tech.c2Body: The light shifts on its own: cool in the morning, golden at night. No switches to decode, no cold glow at midnight.
tech.c3Title: One gesture, the whole room answers.
tech.c3Body: The control layer we specify holds every fixture in agreement. Scenes are composed in advance, so the room arrives complete at a single touch.

where.side: Residential needs scene control. Hospitality needs reliability at scale. Commercial needs adaptability.

projects.introLead: Filter by typology, location or status. Concept studies are labelled as such — we show them because they define the range of the studio, not because we're claiming them as delivered work.
projects.introNote: Every project opens as a full page. Images first, always.

openTitleLines: Your client will never see the drawing.
They'll see the room at eight at night.
services.openBody1: You spend months on the plan, the materials, the proportion. And on handover day none of it gets judged in midday light. It gets judged with the lights on.
services.openBody2: If that light doesn't understand what you drew, the one exposed isn't the supplier. It's you.
services.introLead: We design the light, we protect it through construction, and we stay until it's right. What changes is what the space demands of it.
services.introNote: A jet needs certified components. A tower needs one identity from lobby to penthouse. A yacht needs to survive salt.
services.scopeBody: The three stages are the same across all seven typologies. What changes is what each space demands of you.
services.scopeClose: Every drawing, one closing dossier. Not a set of fragments handed over stage by stage — one complete dossier you can hold us to.

vertical.dossierLead: Not a set of fragments handed over stage by stage — one complete, closeout dossier you can hold us to.

openTitleLines: You chose that material over months.
At eight at night it stops existing.
products.openBody1: Most LEDs dim without warming. At twenty percent they hold the same white they had at a hundred.
products.openBody2: Stone flattens. Wood goes dull. The color you chose in daylight isn't the color your client sees at dinner.
products.openBody3: It isn't a material problem. It's a specification problem.
products.introLead: Every project is built from a short, deliberate list of instruments — fixtures we come back to because they hold their color, survive salt air, and disappear into the ceiling the way the architecture <it>intended.</it>
products.introNote: Not a shop. Photometric files and spec sheets available to specifying professionals, ungated.
products.indepTitle: We don't sell fixtures or represent brands.
products.indepBody: We specify what the project needs. If something better shows up tomorrow, we specify that.

about.introLead: KM Lighting Studio opened in 2023. What it carried inside wasn't new: Karen Mannheim had spent three decades lighting architecture before founding it.
about.introNote: What started with one person knocking on doors in Lima is now a studio with teams in Lima, Miami and Marbella.
about.originTitle: It started by knocking on doors.
about.originBody1: In the early nineties Karen came back to Lima with an idea and no office. She imported fixtures as a rep and knocked on doors — architecture studios, developers, whoever would see her. Two years of that.
about.originBody2: The first office was fifty square meters in Surquillo. The first showroom came seven years later.
about.originBody3: None of that changed when the studio grew. It's still someone walking into a site to see how the light turned out.
about.lead: Karen has delivered more than 2,500 projects across six countries, working alongside studios like RAMSA, Oppenheim and Adriana Hoyos. But the number that matters most isn't on that list: after three decades and that scale, every project is still designed as if it were the only one.
about.throughline: What never changed: here light isn't decoration. It's the soul of the architecture.
about.founderQuote: "I don't design light to be noticed. I design it so the room, the material, the person living there all feel inevitable."
about.founderBody: Karen has spent more than three decades building one of the few lighting practices that works at the level of the world's most demanding architecture firms — and keeps the soul of a studio. She leads the design on every project the studio takes.
about.teamSide: Architecture this complex needs partners who understand the stakes.
about.trazzoNote: Work prior to 2023 delivered under TRAZZO Lighting, directed by Karen Mannheim.

contact.introLead: Whether it's a tower in Lima, an oceanfront house in Florida or a project in Marbella — we'd like to work on projects that ask for light worthy of the architecture.
contact.introNote: Your clients will never know our name. They'll just never want to leave.

cta.body: Whatever stage you're in — concept, tender, or a ceiling that's already closed. We'll tell you honestly if we're the right studio.
cta.bodyServices: Tell us the typology, the stage, and who's on the team. If we're not the right studio for that project, we'll say so on the first call.
cta.bodyTech: If you're specifying and need photometrics, write to us. And if you don't know what to specify yet, even better — that conversation is shorter at the start of a project than at the end.

content.introLead: Thirty-three years of Karen specifying, commissioning and sometimes getting it wrong — written, filmed and talked through with the people who design the buildings.
content.captureBody: Send us the typology and the square meters. We'll tell you what range it falls in before you build the budget.
content.introNote: The articles answer concrete questions. The conversations and walkthroughs are filmed on site, almost always in Spanish.
content.writtenLead: Each piece answers one question, with a number inside. No trend reports.
content.conversationsLead: Karen sits down with architects and interior designers — filmed in their studios, on their sites, in their language.
content.walkthroughsLead: Filmed on site, after handover, at the hour the light was designed for.
content.pressLead: Third-party recognition — the one kind you can't give yourself.
content.featBody: Karen Mannheim among the 50 most powerful women in Peru — recognition of three decades building a lighting studio that now works across six countries.
